source.original_question:
As shown in the figure, a cylinder with a bottom circumference of 24.0, the shortest route that an ant passes along the surface from point A to point B is ()
Choices:
A:12m
B:15m
C:13m
D:14m

adaptations.reason: Specified curved lateral surface and opposite generators, the standard intended interpretation of the source ant-path problem.

independent_solution.method: On the unrolled lateral surface, opposite generators are separated by half the circumference=12m. With vertical difference5m the shortest lateral path is√(12²+5²)=13m.

geometry_notes.visibility_derivation: Viewer has negative y and positive z. Entire top boundary visible; front lower semicircle y<0 visible; rear lower semicircle hidden or source-omitted. Side contours x=+-r,y=0 are analytical tangent generators.
